key_insight: Self-Credit turns sparse outcome rewards into dense training signals by using an agent’s own citations and comparing them across successful and failed rollouts.
engineering_relevance: The method improves credit assignment for long-horizon LLM agents, helping training emphasize actions that contribute to task success.
method: Generate rollout summaries citing earlier turns with critical evidence.
Rescale cited-action credit using agreement and disagreement across rollouts for the same prompt.
Reweight cited-turn advantages with the rescaled credit during RL updates.
evidence_signal: On BrowseComp-Plus, Self-Credit improves Qwen3 8B/32B by 37.0/36.2 points over base models and 8.5/5.6 points over the strongest agentic RL baselines; gains over the strongest baselines are 4.9 points on GAIA and 4.7 on xBench-DeepSearch.
watch_item: Credit quality depends on reliable self-citations and informative rollout comparisons; the abstract does not quantify training overhead.
paper_title: Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling
